name: Guernica
kicker: Picasso’s anti-war mural · Mourns the bombing of a Basque town
briefing: In 1937, German and Italian warplanes bombed the Basque town of Guernica during the Spanish Civil War, an attack that shocked the world. Pablo Picasso answered with a huge black-and-white mural full of pain and protest: a screaming horse, a raging bull, and a mother grieving over her child, with no uniforms or flags in sight. In 1974, a protester even spray-painted “KILL LIES ALL” across the original while it hung at New York’s Museum of Modern Art.

qb.tip: Both Middle School/Easy High School results are genuinely about this painting (no other-meaning noise); a Regular High School retry turned up 6 more, all solid. Watch for the 1974 “KILL LIES ALL” vandalism story, which is about protest art history, not the painting’s own 1937 backstory.

sample.note: 8 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (2 Middle School/Easy High School + 6 Regular High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: Poet Juan Larrea reportedly talked the artist out of making this mural about his own studio, steering him toward the news instead. Commissioned for Spain’s pavilion at the 1937 Paris World’s Fair, the finished oil-on-canvas work measures roughly 11 feet tall and more than 25 feet wide.
tossups.r: This mural is painted almost entirely in black, white, and gray. For 10 points, name this Pablo Picasso work depicting the bombing of a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.

tossups.p: Some viewers see a hidden skull in the nostrils and teeth of a tormented horse near the center of this mural. That horse, pierced through its side, screams above a dismembered soldier whose broken sword sprouts a small flower.
tossups.r: A bare lightbulb shaped like a human eye glares down from the top of the scene. For 10 points, name this huge black-and-white Pablo Picasso mural painted after the 1937 bombing of a Basque town.

tossups.p: A woman on the right of this mural raises her arms in terror, one hand shaped like an airplane as if echoing the bombers overhead, while another woman’s head floats in through a window near the middle. Several figures’ tongues are shaped like knives.
tossups.r: A grieving mother cradles her dead child beneath a bull with a smoking tail. For 10 points, name this Pablo Picasso mural inspired by the bombing of a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.

tossups.p: An arm reaches in through a window of this mural, holding out a flame-lit lamp over the scene below. The work was first exhibited alongside a poem written by Paul Éluard [“ay-lwar”].
tossups.r: A dove appears on a cracked wall beside the bull, where bright light shines through. For 10 points, name this black, white, and gray Pablo Picasso mural depicting the bombing of a Basque town.

tossups.p: A writer named Marrero and the poet Juan Larrea once debated whether its horse or its bull better represented the Spanish people. The horse’s body is textured to look almost like newsprint, as though torn from a wartime newspaper.
tossups.r: A tapestry copy of this mural hanging at the United Nations was covered with a blue curtain before a 2003 speech by Colin Powell. For 10 points, name this Pablo Picasso work depicting the bombing of a Basque town.

tossups.p: In 1974, artist Tony Shafrazi [“shuh-FRAH-zee”] spray-painted the words “KILL LIES ALL” across this mural, a protest later tied to the Vietnam War’s My Lai Massacre. A tapestry copy of it normally hangs at the United Nations.
tossups.r: This mural blends Picasso’s fractured Cubist shapes with dreamlike Surrealist distortion. For 10 points, name this black-and-white work painted after the 1937 bombing of a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.

tossups.p: This mural’s bull stands over the wreckage with a smoking, flame-tipped tail; some read the animal as a symbol of Spain itself or of Fascism. Just beneath it, a grieving mother cradles her dead child.
tossups.r: A screaming horse, pierced through its side, dominates the center of the scene. For 10 points, name this huge Pablo Picasso mural depicting the bombing of a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.

tossups.p: Nazi German and Fascist Italian warplanes carried out the real-life attack shown in this mural, which was commissioned for a pavilion at the 1937 Paris World’s Fair. Painted almost entirely in black, white, and gray, it combines Cubist fragmentation with Surrealist nightmare imagery.
tossups.r: A dismembered soldier lies at the bottom of the scene, his broken sword sprouting a small flower. For 10 points, name this Pablo Picasso mural depicting the bombing of a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.

tossups.p: A tapestry copy of this mural at the United Nations was covered with a blue curtain before a 2003 speech about Iraq, and in 1974 a protester spray-painted “KILL LIES ALL” across the original. A bare lightbulb shaped like a human eye glares from the top of the scene.
tossups.r: A screaming horse and a bull with a smoking tail loom over a dismembered soldier’s broken sword. For 10 points, name this black-and-white Pablo Picasso mural of a bombed Basque town.

tossups.p: This mural’s grieving mother weeps beneath a bull that some see as a symbol of Fascism, while a screaming horse rears above a soldier’s broken sword, from which a small flower grows.
tossups.r: Painted in black, white, and gray, it was commissioned for Spain’s pavilion at the 1937 Paris World’s Fair. For 10 points, name this Pablo Picasso mural depicting the bombing of a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.

tossups.p: An eye-shaped lightbulb glares down over a screaming horse and a smoking-tailed bull in this mural, while a dismembered soldier below grips a broken sword sprouting a flower. Nazi German and Fascist Italian planes carried out the attack this work depicts.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this black-and-white Pablo Picasso mural painted after the 1937 bombing of a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.

tossups.p: Hanging today in Madrid’s Museo Reina Sofía [“RAY-nah soh-FEE-ah”], this mural shows a bull with a burning tail standing near a grieving mother and her dead child.
tossups.r: A screaming horse looms over a dismembered soldier whose broken sword sprouts a flower, all beneath an eye-shaped lightbulb. For 10 points, name this huge Pablo Picasso mural depicting the bombing of a Basque town.

tossups.p: This mural shows no uniforms and no flags, only a screaming horse, a bull with a smoking tail, and a dismembered soldier whose broken sword sprouts a flower, all under a lightbulb shaped like a human eye.
tossups.r: Considered one of history’s most powerful anti-war paintings, it was painted by Pablo Picasso in black, white, and gray. For 10 points, name this mural depicting the 1937 bombing of a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.

tossups.p: A grieving mother and a dismembered soldier appear beneath a screaming horse and a bull with a smoking tail in this mural, whose creator reportedly refused to explain its symbols.
tossups.r: Nazi German and Fascist Italian warplanes carried out the real bombing shown in this work. For 10 points, name this black-and-white Pablo Picasso mural depicting the attack on a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.

tossups.p: A screaming horse and a bull with a smoking tail stand over a dismembered soldier whose broken sword sprouts a small flower in this huge black-and-white mural.
tossups.r: Nazi German and Fascist Italian warplanes bombed the titular Basque town while this mural’s creator was living in Paris. For 10 points, name this 1937 work by Pablo Picasso.

trap.title: Painting or painter?
trap.body: Quiz bowl always wants the title of the artwork, not its creator. A tossup that says “name this painting” or “name this mural” wants the title, not Pablo Picasso, even though every single clue describes a choice Picasso made. The painting is also sometimes confused with Picasso’s other 1937 response to the same war, _The Weeping Woman_, a related but separate work.
trap.fix: Listen for “painting,” “mural,” or “work” — that always means the title. If the question instead asks “who painted…,” the answer is Picasso, not the title.
